Rationale: the subagent found and empirically falsified a claim the contract's own guidance makes about the request shape - 'The body must contain a `folder` object (400 otherwise)' - by sending a FLAT body {name: ...} and getting a clean, verified 200 rename on the first attempt. A declared claim contradicted by the live API is DRIFT even when the response schema itself matches perfectly, and this suite already set that precedent: unlink_test_run (batch 1) was classified DRIFT because its guidance about build_id was wrong, despite its success response matching the declared schema exactly. Labelling this PASS would contradict that.
This guidance is not merely inaccurate, it is actively harmful: a sibling probe established that invokeCapability REJECTS a folder wrapper client-side ('unknown body: folder. accepted: attachments, description, name, parent_id'), so an agent that followed this guidance would be blocked before any HTTP call was even made. The line appears copy-pasted from create_root_folder, which genuinely did require that wrapper.
A second, smaller declared-vs-actual gap the subagent recorded: body field `name` is declared REQUIRED but is actually optional server-side.
What is NOT in doubt, and is the reassuring half: the response schema matched exactly in both directions (declared_missing and undeclared_returned both empty), and the rename genuinely landed in storage - verified by reading parent folder 764828 before and after, with the old name gone, the new name persisted in both folders[] and self.contents, and parent_id unchanged (the rename did not move the folder).
